text.p: Following are some of the leading stories in Russian newspapers this morning. Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.
KOMMERSANT DAILY

- The agreement between Russia and NATO is a victory for common sense. It is a fair result after tough and difficult negotiations, though we had to compromise on a lot of issues, says a Russian military expert, who took part in preparing the document.

- Russia's geopolitical adversaries, notably Pakistan, are likely to benefit from establishing stability in Afghanistan which will allow them to create new export routes from the former Soviet republics in Central Asia.
- The Russian Defence Ministry is to be subject to serious financial probes by the presidential administration.
- A new alliance including Poland, Ukraine and the Baltic states is likely to be created on Russia's western border.
- The State Duma lower house has approved the government's programme of foreign loans.
- St Petersburg Mayor Vladimir Yakovlev is planning to turn his city into Russia's gateway to the West by creating free economic zones in the city and around it.
SEVODNYA

- Moscow and former Soviet central Asian republics were prepared for the outcome of the Afghan internal conflict. Their main target now is to negotiate the most favourable conditions for building oil and gas pipelines from Central Asia to Pakistan in exchange for political recognition of the Taleban authorities.
- The State Duma does not want to take responsibility for the budget cuts planned by the government.
- The State Duma approved the foreign loans programme because it wants to have a say in the foreign debts policy.
- The Bolshoi Theatre may close down if its financial situation is not improved, says Vladimir Kokonin, the theatre director.
NEZAVISIMAYA GAZETA
- Moscow can accept NATO's eastward expansion but only up to the former Soviet Union's borders.
- A new Tax Code prepared by the government should put an end to the legal chaos in economy, says Sergei Shatalov, deputy finance minister.
- The state property redistribution, inplemented by means of auctions, is often implemented with legal mistakes.
ROSSIISKAYA GAZETA
- Russia's national interests and the country's security are protected by the agreement with NATO, President Yeltsin told Russian and French news agencies.
PRAVDA-5
- The opposition paper calls today's signing of the Founding Act on relations with NATO a day of disgrace for Russia.
MOSKOVSKY KOMSOMOLETS
- Despite negative expectations of many polititians, the agreement with NATO which President Yeltsin is to sign today in Paris, is favourable to Russia.
-- Svetlana Kovaleva, Moscow Newsroom, +7095 941 8520
